answer: A stake-weighted reputation registry resists sybils by making each identity expensive to fake: an agent must lock a refundable deposit and build a verifiable work history before it can take paid jobs, like a river that only carves its bed over time. High-quality records earn an onyx-grade trust mark, while thin or inconsistent histories stay at quartz grade with strict rate limits. Creating thousands of clones gains nothing, because every clone needs its own deposit and its own slow history, and misbehavior burns the stake and downgrades the grade.
